results.text: The base station could not deliver events to the cloud. Frontline action: verify internet access, restart router and base station, set router DNS to automatic. If E-503 persists after these steps while the base station is online, escalate to FAE (cloud channel or certificate issue).

Base station online, live view works on local network, but no event notifications; E-503 every few minutes. Router restart and DNS reset did not help. Escalated; expired device certificate on backend. Escalated correctly.

Escalate when any of the following holds: (1) two or more peripherals fail at the same time while the base station is online; (2) a firmware or protocol mismatch remains after an OTA attempt or OTA is not possible; (3) the standard frontline fix was executed and the problem persists; (4) the app's device list and the base station binding table disagree; (5) a device fails even next to the base station after a factory reset.

complaint: Local live view works fine on my home Wi-Fi, but I haven't received a single push notification since Tuesday, and when I'm out I can't see any clips. I rebooted the router, then the base station, and even set my router's DNS to automatic like the help article said. Still nothing. I've been on hold with my ISP and they insist the internet is fine.
usability_reason: The response is clear and polite, and it avoids claiming unperformed checks or fixes. However, actionability is limited: it only says an engineer will follow up and provides no next steps or timeline. The session record shows no questions asked and no actions performed, yet the response references customer-performed reboots and DNS changes as if verified; those are not supported by the session record, which weakens the claim discipline. The root-cause label is plausible but not independently verified, and the response does not overclaim a fix.
